name: Small Craft Frames
description: Community frames published by Small Craft.

items.name: Calendar
items.description: A simple shared calendar, unique per placement. Space editors add events on a given day or set them to repeat weekly (for example every Mon/Wed/Fri at 3pm) until an end date or forever, each with an optional time, length, color, link, and note; everyone else sees a clean read-only view, including anyone the space owner shares the frame publicly with. Switch between a month grid and a week view with events laid out by time of day. Timed events are authored in your own time zone and automatically shifted to each viewer's local time, so everyone sees the right moment wherever they are. Recurring events can be deleted just for one day, from a day onward, or entirely, and an event's link opens in the native browser (or a new tab on the web). The view also adapts to its size — the full month/week views when there's room, and a compact upcoming-events agenda once the tile gets small, so it stays usable down to about 200×200. The whole calendar lives in a single JSON file in a per-placement folder. No database or sync tables.

items.name: Checklist
items.description: A simple, collaborative to-do list. Each placement is its own list — any member of the space can add tasks, cycle each task through three states (unstarted, in-progress, complete), drag to reorder, and delete. Non-members get a live read-only view. Items, ordering, and states are stored in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement, and every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Community Home
items.description: A minimal website builder for a community home page. Admins configure the title, color, sections, and links; anonymous visitors see the published public page.

items.name: Community Library
items.description: Track items shared by a community — books, tools, gear — and who has them checked out. Items and members live in shared SyncTables (the members table is compatible with Member Manager so the same roster can be reused). Per-placement preferences (org name, borrow durations, owner-only edit) are stored in a local JSON file.

items.name: Discussion Channel
items.description: A per-placement realtime chat channel. Members chat, react with Phosphor Light icons, and delete their own messages; owners can rename the channel, pick a theme, and choose whether Viewer-role members can participate. Non-members, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, read the channel live without posting.

items.name: File Folder
items.description: A simple shared file bucket, unique per placement. Members (or just the owner — the owner chooses) can add files by clicking 'Add file' or dragging them in from the desktop. The owner sets who may add files, a max file size, and a max number of files. Anyone who can open the frame can list and download its files, so sharing the frame publicly shares the folder. Files live in the frame's own data folder in a per-placement subfolder; only the owner's sharing preferences are stored, in a single JSON file. No database or sync tables.

items.name: ASCII Runner
items.description: A retro side-scrolling ASCII game where you jump over rocks and duck under birds. Use arrow keys to survive as long as you can!

items.name: Dice Roller
items.description: Simple dice roller. Roll via the UI or HTTP API; result is broadcast to all viewers of a frame instance.

items.name: Pancake Stacker
items.description: Simple solo arcade game. A pancake swings back and forth at the top of the griddle — tap, click, or hit space to drop it onto the stack. Each pancake trims to the overlap with the one below, so the tower narrows as you climb. Miss entirely and the stack topples. High score per placement.

items.name: Garden Gnome
items.description: An at-a-glance helper for home gardeners. Set a location, pick your soil, tick the plants you grow, and Garden Gnome fetches local weather (Open-Meteo, keyless) every 15 minutes — past 5 days plus the next 24 hours — and shows three color-coded dots on a +/- spectrum next to each plant for water, temperature, and sunlight so you know when a plant is being naturally pampered or stressed. Space editors set the garden up; everyone else, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, gets the same read-only board with the location withheld.

items.name: Help Desk
items.description: Anonymous visitors submit a message with email (plus admin-configured fields); known users in the space see a realtime inbox of incoming correspondence.

items.name: Kanban Board
items.description: A drag-and-drop task board, unique per placement. Space editors organize work as cards in channel-colored columns: add, rename, recolor, and reorder columns, drag cards between them, and keep details and a short label on each card. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees a live read-only view of the board. Cards and columns live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement, and every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Market Weather
items.description: A turnout forecaster for outdoor commerce — farmers markets, festivals, food trucks, street vendors, walkable storefronts. Set a location and Market Weather pulls 72 hours of weather from Open-Meteo (keyless), compares it against the last 30 days' local norms, and folds in temperature comfort, rain, UV, daylight, wind, weekend bonus, and time-of-day into a single composite turnout curve. The graph overlays each contributing factor as a faint band (daytime in pale yellow, rain in blue rising from the bottom, extreme heat/cold in red, weekend bonus in green) so you can see at a glance WHY the bold turnout line moves the way it does — and plan how much to stock, bake, or brew for the days ahead.

items.name: Member Manager
items.description: View and manage a roster of people and their roles within an organization, including an optional phone number for each member. Member entries are stored in a shared SyncTable so every space member sees the same list. Email is a one-tap mailto link; a phone number offers a call/text chooser. Per-placement preferences (org name, available roles, edit policy) are stored in a local JSON file.

items.name: Member Reachout
items.description: Send updates and notifications to the people in your roster. Reads the same shared Members SyncTable as the Member Manager frame (bind it to the same table when prompted), so names, roles, emails and optional phone numbers stay in one place. Compose a message, pick who hears it (a role, several roles, or everyone), then send it as one bcc email or hand-text everyone with a phone number — one tap at a time. Every send is logged locally (date, audience, method) so you can browse the backlog and re-send later. Non-members, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, see the message history for whichever roles you choose to expose.

items.name: Outpost
items.description: A lightweight public posting board for sharing with the world. Space members (editors) publish short posts — a passing thought, an open question, a status update, an announcement, a quick poll, or an image / audio / video clip — and anyone with the frame's share link can read them. Each post shows its author and the time it was shared, and URLs in the text become clickable (opened safely in the reader's browser). Posts live entirely in the frame's own data folder: one subfolder per placement holds a encrypted LocalTable (posts, media rows, and poll votes — indexed so a large, active feed stays fast) plus a per-post subfolder for any attached media bytes. Local file only, no sync tables.

items.name: Picture Frame
items.description: A digital picture frame for a space. Space editors drop photos in — by clicking Add or dragging them from the desktop — and everyone sees them as a grid of thumbnails; tap one and it fills the frame, tap again to go back. Turn on slideshow mode and the frame cycles through the photos at an interval you choose. There is one shared display: whatever an editor puts up is what every viewer sees, and the frame remembers exactly what it was showing, so a restarted frame or a rebooted machine comes back to the same photo. Viewer-role members and anonymous link visitors can browse the photos on their own screen without changing what the frame displays for anyone else. Photos are downscaled on the way in and stored with their bytes on the host beside a per-placement encrypted LocalTable; nothing leaves the device.

items.name: Roadmap
items.description: A simple, robust project roadmapping tool — one roadmap per placement. Set a project name, overview, and quick links; break the work into milestones with target dates; and track dozens of small tasks per milestone through three states (unstarted, in-progress, complete), claiming and checking them off as you go. Drag tasks between milestones (or the Back Burner / Maybe Later buckets) to reprioritize, and within a milestone to rank them. Collapsed milestone headers still show live counts and a completed-per-day burn rate; a Timeline view lays out upcoming milestones with days-remaining and overdue color-coding. A milestone can only be marked done once all its tasks are complete. Everything is stored in a lightweight per-placement encrypted LocalTable database on the host and pushed live to every viewer; non-members get a read-only view.

items.name: Roundtable
items.description: A per-placement discussion + two prioritized idea boards for a space. Members chat in a single channel, add items to a Positives list (features/tasks) or a Negatives list (issues/bugs), and +1 the ones that matter. Items are ranked by votes, then recency. Only the owner can rename the frame and set high-level preferences. Non-members, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, follow along in a live read-only view.

items.name: Seamdeck
items.description: A tiny game console for your space. The frame is the whole device: a handheld on narrow screens, a TV + controller on wide ones. Members open sessions of little Phosphor-icon games (shot put, regatta, hot slice), join each other's lobbies, take turns or race in realtime, and chase the shared high-score board. Controls: D-pad via arrows/WASD, O = primary, I = secondary/back. It's also a template — each game is a self-contained two-file cartridge, and the console gives every cartridge lobbies, turn rotation, realtime racing, spectators, results, and high scores for free, so forking it into your own console is mostly writing games.

items.name: Slideshow
items.description: A simple presentation maker and presenter, unique per placement. Space editors build a deck of slides — stylized text (headings, body, bullet lists), uploaded images, and shapes — laid out freely on a fixed slide canvas; everything is positioned and sized proportionally so the deck looks identical from a 300×300 tile up to a scaled-up fullscreen presentation. Viewers can browse and present the deck but cannot edit it. The deck follows the space's channel color; a few show-wide settings (background, slide aspect, and an optional "keep viewers in sync" mode that locks every viewer's presentation to the editor's current slide) sit alongside the slides. The whole deck lives in a single JSON file in a per-placement folder, with uploaded images (auto-resized to keep file sizes reasonable) stored beside it. No database or sync tables.

items.name: Space Radio
items.description: A synced web radio player for everyone in a space. Space editors pick a station from a large list of public web stations — rock, pop, ambient, jazz, French, Italian, Australian, NPR, chiptune, and more — and everyone else, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, listens along to the same audio simultaneously. Play/pause and station selection are shared; each viewer's volume and mute are local and remembered between sessions.

items.name: Watercolor Studio
items.description: A quiet, beautiful place to paint with watercolors. Each placement is its own sheet of textured paper. Pigments are real watercolor pans — pick one, or add bits of several into the mixing well and they blend subtractively the way paint actually does (blue plus yellow makes green, complements make mud). A range of brushes (broad wash, round, flat, dry-brush, fine detail) lay translucent washes that pool, bleed, and darken at their edges; layered strokes glaze over one another. A clean-water Lift brush pulls pigment back out. Optional thin guide outlines (a pear, a teacup, a koi, a mountain lake…) sit faintly beneath the paint so new painters can trace as they learn. Editors in the space paint together in real time; anonymous viewers watch read-only. The whole painting is stored as deterministic vector strokes in a single JSON file per placement — no database, no network.

items.name: Weather Info
items.description: Example weather info/forecast using keyless API (open meteo)
